title: Site Coverage Area and Building Height Under QCVN 01:2026
desc: QCVN 01:2026 from 2027: site coverage excludes canopies and awnings; how height is measured; a maximum land-use coefficient of 7; spacing between buildings.
summary: Explains how site coverage area, building height, the land-use coefficient and spacing between buildings are calculated under QCVN 01:2026/BXD, applicable from 1 January 2027.
body: p

QCVN 01:2026/BXD, issued with Circular 46/2026/TT-BXD, takes effect on 1 January 2027. Many indicators such as building density, setbacks and spacing between houses depend on how site coverage area and building height are calculated. This article explains these concepts under Section 1.4 of the Regulation.
h2
1. Site coverage area: what is excluded?
p
Site coverage area is the area of the horizontal projection of the whole building on the site (Section 1.4.19). The following are not counted in site coverage area:
ul

Open ancillary works: gates, fences, decorative landscape features, outdoor swimming pools, outdoor parking lots, outdoor sports courts, guard houses, access ways, covered basement ventilation elements, technical infrastructure works, and non-permanent works.

Gutters, canopies, eaves, awnings, entrance steps, sills, escape stairs and bridge corridors – if they meet fire safety and construction safety requirements, do not obstruct circulation, and are not combined with another use.
p
Net building density = site coverage area ÷ land plot area (Section 1.4.20).
h2
2. Land-use coefficient: how many square meters of floor may be built?
p

The land-use coefficient is the ratio (in times) of total floor area, including basements, to the site area; excluding all floor area for technical systems, fire prevention and fighting, refuge areas and parking (Section 1.4.22). For a detached house plot, this coefficient does not exceed 7 times (Note 1 to Table 8, Section 2.5.3.1).
p

Example: a 100 m² plot has a maximum building density of 90% under Table 8, so site coverage area may not exceed 90 m²; a maximum land-use coefficient of 7 corresponds to total floor area counted for the coefficient of no more than 700 m². This is the limit of the Regulation; the specific indicators for each plot (usually lower) are set by detailed planning and urban design.
h2
3. Where is building height measured from?
p

Building height is measured vertically from the lowest ground level under the approved planning within the site coverage area to the highest point of the building, including a penthouse or pitched roof (Section 1.4.26). Not counted: antenna masts, lightning rods, solar energy equipment, water tanks, chimneys, vent pipes and decorative architectural details.
p

Height determines the minimum setback by road width (Table 7) – a house under 19 m high has a minimum setback of 0 at every road width. For details see Building density and setbacks for houses under QCVN 01:2026.
h2
4. Spacing between buildings
p
The minimum spacing between buildings is set by detailed planning and urban design, and must also meet the following (Section 2.5.1), for buildings under 46 m high:
ul
Between the long sides of buildings: not less than 1/2 the building height and not less than 7 m;
Between a gable end and another gable end or long side of another building: not less than 1/3 of the height and not less than 4 m;
Rows of adjoining houses on the same plot that are planned to be separated: the distance between the rear sides is not less than 4 m.
p

In existing areas that cannot meet this, the spacing is determined by detailed planning or urban design but must ensure fire prevention and fighting, firefighting vehicle access roads at least 4 m wide, and natural ventilation and lighting for every building (Section 2.6.5).
h2
5. How does this apply to your house?
p

The Regulation is a tool for state agencies to check the indicators in planning (Section 5.1). Planning approved before 1 January 2027 continues to be implemented until the end of its term, and when adjusted it must follow the new regulation (Section 5.4.1). The indicators applicable to a land plot are shown in the planning information and the construction permit – see how to obtain planning information.
note

This article is only a summary for reference and does not replace legal documents. QCVN 01:2026/BXD (Circular 46/2026/TT-BXD) is effective from 1 January 2027, replacing QCVN 01:2021/BXD. The specific indicators for each land plot follow detailed planning, urban design and the local architectural management regulations.
